the gut microbial communities of honey bees performing different behavioural roles in the colony were significantly different, with core taxa showing different relative abundance in bees performing different tasks.

the gut microbial community of worker honey bees performing different behavioural (foraging vs nest tasks) is different, suggesting that the gut microbial community may play a role in the social behavioural traits of honey bees.
the honey bee gut microbiome differs between bees that perform foraging and nest tasks.

how honey bee behaviour is related to the gut microbiome and how this may be important in the ecology of honey bee colonies.
understanding how the honey bee gut microbiome is related to the social behaviour of worker bees.
the role of gut microbiota in social insect ecology and evolution.

the gut microbial community is associated with behavioural tasks of the workers in honey bees.
we found that the gut microbiome of honey bees is associated, at least in part, with the task that they perform.
the gut microbiome is indeed associated with behavioural task.

the honey bee gut microbiome is influenced by social behaviour and the associated local environment exposure.
the gut microbiome is not only associated with the behavioural task in honey bee but also the environment and the diet.

honey bee behavioural task is associated with gut microbial community composition.
